extracted.intended_audience: zoologists, taxonomists, museum curators and naturalists working on freshwater sponge systematics
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed taxonomic description and diagnosis of freshwater sponge species (morphology, spicules, gemmules, habitat, distribution, biology) intended to identify, distinguish, and document species and varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponge external morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the whole sponge: form (soft, fragile, amorphous, massive, flat, lichenoid, branching or unbranched), surface features (smooth, ridged, cockscomb-like), oscula (size, shape, raised or not, surrounded by collars or radiating furrows), canals (broad vertical or horizontal canals), inhalent pores and external membrane, colour and smell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use characters such as presence/absence and form of oscula (e.g. 'large, deep, round oscula' in S. carteri; 'numerous, small, flat, distinctly star-shaped' oscula in S. fragilis), surface sculpture (ridged vs smooth), and canal orientation (broad vertical vs wide horizontal channels) as primary diagnostic features. Note that form may vary with attachment substrate and water movement (e.g. specimens swayed by wind show undulating ridges). Record whether specimens were alive or dead when collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of the skeleton: presence and character of radiating fibres and transverse fibres (their fineness, spacing, whether transverse fibres are far apart or splayed), compactness or diffuseness of skeleton, amount of spongin, and whether gemmules are caged by skeleton-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe whether skeleton is diffuse or compact, number of parallel spicules in radiating fibres, spacing of transverse fibres, splaying of transverse fibres (e.g. 'transverse fibres splayed out at either end so that they sometimes resemble a pair of fans joined together by the handles'). Note amount of spongin (none, moderate, or present) since this differentiates taxa and varieties (e.g. var. mollis paucity of skeleton-spicules → very delicate radiating/transverse fibres).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton-spicules (morphology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form of main skeletal spicules: smooth or ornamented, slender or stout, pointed at both ends or blunt, straight or feebly curved, sometimes constricted and expanded to resemble spear-heads; presence/absence of flesh-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record shape, tip form, curvature and ornamentation; these characters often distinguish species (e.g. S. carteri 'skeleton-spicules smooth, pointed, nearly straight' vs forms with sparsely spined skeleton-spicules). Note whether immature skeleton-spicules can be mistaken for flesh-spicules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule-spicules (morphology and ornament)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmule-spicules described as cylindrical, constricted in the middle, blunt or pointed, clothed with short sharp straight spines or with irregular circle(s) of strong straight or recurved spines at ends resembling rudimentary rotules; spines distribution (more numerous/longer at ends or equally distributed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe shaft ornament (short straight spines vs longer terminal spines forming rudimentary rotules), whether gemmule-spicules are free in the parenchyma, and variability in length and spine-arrangement. Use these features to separate closely allied species (e.g. S. hemephydatia's gemmule-spicules 'ornamented with shorter spines, which are more numerous and longer at the ends than at the middle' distinguishes it from relatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule coat, membrane and internal arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure of the gemmule: granular cellular coat (thick, several layers), presence of polygonal air-spaces with chitinous walls, an external chitinous membrane which may pucker in preserved specimens, arrangement of spicules in the granular coat (horizontal, upright, irregular), and whether gemmules are free or adherent to support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether gemmules are 'numerous, small, free, spherical, yellow, with a well-developed granular coat' or bound together in layers; whether spicules are arranged almost horizontally or more vertical; and whether there is 'no external layer of horizontal spicules.' These characters are diagnostic at subgeneric and species levels (e.g. Eunapius: gemmules covered with layers of distinct polygonal air-spaces). Note preservation artifacts (external coat puckering).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foraminal tubule characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Number, position and shape of foraminal tubules on gemmules: at least one straight conical tubule, often two (one at top and one at one side), tube shape (straight, conical, wide but delicate, bottle-shaped inverted bottle, short, projecting or curved), and relation to a crater-like depression or rampart in the granular coat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and describe tubule length, thickness and curvature; note whether tubules project beyond the cellular coat or are contained within a crater-like depression. Tubule form (e.g. 'inverted bottle' or 'short straight foraminal tubule') is species-distinctive and may be broken off in dried specimens, so check preservation state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule arrangement and adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Mode of gemmule occurrence: adherent to support forming a pavement layer one gemmule thick, bound together in free groups forming a flat basal layer, or free and independent within the sponge; sometimes forming cages of skeleton-spicules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether gemmules are 'firmly adherent to the support at the base' or 'bound together in free groups' (as in S. fragilis); arrangement helps separate taxa (e.g. adherent gemmules with multiple apertures and rough external surface distinguish certain subgenera).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurements of spicules and gemmules
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numerical ranges for lengths and diameters of skeleton-spicules, free microscleres, gemmule-spicules, and gemmule diameter (given in mm, e.g. 'Length of skeleton-spicules 0.289-0.374 mm; greatest diameter of skeleton-spicules 0.012-0.016 mm; length of free microscleres 0.08-0.096 mm; diameter of gemmule 0.272-0.374 mm').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurements with units and ranges, ideally from type or representative specimens. Include magnification at which figures are drawn (e.g. '× 240', '× 140') and specify whether measurements are of optical sections. Use consistent units (mm) and indicate variation across specimens/varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type specimen and repository citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation of type specimen or types and their depositories (e.g. 'TYPE in the collection of the Indian Museum', 'TYPES in the United States National Museum; co-types in Calcutta', British Museum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always state the presumed type specimen, its museum repository and any co-types. This is essential for nomenclatural stability and for future comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat and microhabitat
rubrics_metrics.description: Exact habitat where specimens occur: type of water (fresh, slightly brackish), substrate (roots of shrubs, weeds, stones, walls of wells), depth/position (surface, bottom, attached to stems), and seasonal occurrence (dates, months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record environmental context (e.g. 'backwater near Shasthancottah, in slightly brackish water; on the roots of shrubs' or 'growing on weeds at the edge of the Sur Lake') and note whether specimens were alive when collected. Habitat often correlates with colour and form and is useful in diagnosing varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the known geographic range and specific localities, including countries, regions, localities, islands, and altitudinal occurrences (e.g. lists of localities across India, Burma, Ceylon, North America, Europe, Africa, islands like Andaman and Madura).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both broad biogeographic notes ('cosmopolitan', 'widely distributed in North America') and precise locality records with collectors' names and dates when known. Note surprising occurrences (e.g. oceanic island records) and degrees of identification certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology and reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on life history: modes of reproduction (gemmule formation, sexual reproduction, budding/regeneration from torn pieces), timing (seasonality: cold weather onset, March/November), germination behaviour (in situ germination, floating/dried gemmules, response to temperature), and developmental observations (differentiation, spicule secretion, osculum formation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe all observed reproductive modalities and their seasonal timing; document experimental observations (e.g. small sponge pieces forming young sponges in ca. ten days). Note that gemmules produced in different seasons or conditions may differ (e.g. gemmules lacking gemmule-spicules in aquaria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Species diagnosis and distinguishing features
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit comparative characters used to separate the species from allied taxa: e.g. 'adherent gemmules with their (usually) multiple apertures and rough external surface' distinguish a species from Euspongilla; 'upright and regular arrangement of gemmule-spicules' distinguishes S. crateriformis and S. hemephydatia; S. carteri 'readily distinguished from all other Indian freshwater sponges by its large, deep, round oscula.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concise differential diagnoses against nearest allies, emphasizing unique or combined characters (gives examples and comparisons). Note where characters are intermediate between genera and justify taxonomic placement (e.g. systematic position intermediate between Euspongilla and Ephydatia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraspecific variation and varietal status
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition and description of varieties/subspecies within a species based on differences such as paucity of skeleton-spicules (var. mollis), canal/oscula structure (var. cava), or growth-form (var. lobosa); discussion of whether these forms are true varieties, subspecies, or environmental phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether morphological differences are consistent geographically or may be environmentally induced (e.g. silica deficiency hypothesis, association with luxuriant vegetation). Avoid premature splitting: consider frequency, co-occurrence with typical form, and environmental correlates when deciding taxonomic status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental influence on morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements on how local environmental factors (temperature, brackish infiltration, vegetation type, mud composition) may influence sponge colour, spicule production and form (e.g. black sponges turning white in clean water, soft forms in ponds with luxuriant vegetation, possible silica deficiency affecting spicule production).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record environmental parameters and consider them when interpreting morphological characters; perform comparative sampling across habitats to test hypotheses of environmentally induced variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated fauna and ecological interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: List and roles of animals associated with the sponge: sheltering crustacea (isopods like Tachæa spongillicola), larval insects (Sisyra indica), flatworms, prawn predators (Palæmon lamarrei), chironomid larvae (some beneficial as commensals), polyzoans embedded in sponge, small fishes using oscula for egg deposition, and worms that assist gemmule release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note both potentially harmful and beneficial associates and their behaviours (feeding, sheltering, tube-building). These associations can affect sponge condition, reproduction and dispersal and may be diagnostic of particular sponge habitats or varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and artifact considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of preservation on morphology: external chitinous membrane puckers in preserved specimens, foraminal tubules liable to be broken off in dried specimens, colour changes in alcohol (liquids turning dark brown and staining alcohol and sponge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record preservation method and state at examination; interpret delicate structures (tubules, thin membranes) cautiously if dried or preserved. When possible examine living material or well-preserved specimens for diagnostic characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen observation and illustration practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to illustrate spicules and gemmules with magnification annotations (e.g. figures at ×240, ×140, optical sections), and to examine spicules both in situ (parenchyma) and after freeing them for measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide photographs/line drawings with stated magnification, note whether figures derive from type specimens or local material, and indicate variability by showing more than one exemplar when spicule shape is variable. Record whether gemmule-spicules are found free in parenchyma or arranged in coat when describing species.
